newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. senator raises doubts on amendment vote.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. senator raises doubts on amendment vote.

text.p: Senator Mary Landrieu, one of two pivotal Democratic votes on the balanced budget constitutional amendment, Monday expressed deep concern about voting for the Senate's Republican version.

Landrieu's opposition could kill the balanced budget amendment because it would give Democrats the 34th vote needed to defeat it. She told reporters two Democratic alternatives to be considered by the Senate dealt with her concerns for Social Security and the need for a federal capital budget.
"I am committed to vote for an amendment but I did not commit to a particular version," she said.
A vote against the Republican version would likely be the fatal blow as the Democratic alternatives were not expected to pick up enough Republican support to pass both the House and Senate.

Landrieu said she felt comfortable that Louisiana voters would understand if she voted against the Republican version. However, she said she would probably announce her decision Tuesday or Wednesday. "My constituents want me to vote for the best version," she said.

In discussing the issue of Social Security, the senator said she was disturbed that the retirement trust fund was not operating as one. "It is not a good practice now, and locking it in the Constitution makes matters worse," she said.
The Senate will vote on several proposals to exempt Social Security trust funds from the budget deficit calculation.
Senate Republican leaders intend to go forward with a final vote either this week or next, no matter what the expected outcome, a Republican source said.
One other Democratic freshman, New Jersey's Robert Torricelli, has not announced his decision.
